key_insight: DepthWeave-KV makes long-context inference cheaper by compressing KV caches in a token-aware way, instead of forcing every token and layer to share the same memory budget. It preserves important retrieval signals by factorizing neighboring transformer-layer states with shared low-rank bases while adapting what gets kept per token.
problem_solved: Long-context language models are bottlenecked by the large memory and bandwidth cost of storing key-value (KV) caches. Existing compression methods often use uniform budgets across layers or tokens, which can hurt performance when different tokens need different amounts of lexical or semantic detail preserved.
method: Factorizes key and value states across neighboring transformer layers using shared low-rank channel bases.
Applies token-adaptive compression so important tokens can retain more information than less critical ones.
Targets KV cache reduction while trying to preserve retrieval quality for both lexical cues and semantic state.
impact: This approach can help practitioners run longer-context models more efficiently on limited hardware by reducing KV-cache memory pressure. It is especially relevant for production inference settings where latency, throughput, and context length all matter.

paper_title: DepthWeave-KV: Token-Adaptive Cross-Layer Residual Factorization for Long-Context KV Cache Compression
paper_authors: Anna Cordoba, Adam Puente Tercero, Nerea Angulo Hijo, Mar Linares Tercero, Julia Barrientos
